findings.title: DPTrainer blesses mf_band + sampling_mode="poisson", which pairs the BandMF cyclic-Poisson accountant with a plain full-dataset PoissonSampler — violating the hypothesis of the cited Choquette-Choo et al. Theorem 4
findings.claim: `_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS["mf_band"] = frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})` (_training_arguments.py:188) with the comment at :182-184 "``mf_band`` accepts ``\"poisson\"`` as a looser-but-valid alternative to its canonical ``\"b_min_sep\"`` participation pattern". Under that setting `build_amplifier_factory(sampling_mode="poisson", strategy=BandMfStrategy(bands=b))` returns `ftrl_acc.poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), ...)` = `CyclicPoisson`, whose `pld_at` composes only `num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands)` per-group Poisson-Gaussian PLDs at `effective_nm = nm / ||coef|| = nm / 1.0` (_poisson.py:178-188), while `build_sampler(sampling_mode="poisson", ...)` returns the DP-SGD `PoissonSampler` over the WHOLE dataset every step (_dpftrl.py:224-233, imported from `opaque.dpsgd.sampling` at :46-50) — `bands` is never passed. The accounting module cites this analysis to "BandMF amplification: Choquette-Choo et al. (2023) https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08153" (_poisson.py:16). That paper's Theorem 4 reads: "Suppose C is b-banded and lower triangular, and the examples participating in each step are chosen according to Algorithm 2. Then BandMF satisfies any standard DP guarantee satisfied by performing k sensitivity-kappa queries on a dataset of size m-check = floor(m/b) using the Gaussian mechanism" — Algorithm 2 being the cyclic partition "D_1,...,D_b <- arbitrary partition of D. for i=1..n do j = i (mod b). S_i <- random size B subset of D_j." A plain full-dataset Poisson sampler is not Algorithm 2 (nor its Appendix-F Poisson generalisation): an example is eligible on EVERY round, so its participations are not b-separated and its contributions land in overlapping row-blocks of the b-banded C. The decomposition into ceil(n/b) independent subsampled Gaussians that CyclicPoisson.pld_at performs therefore has no proof behind it in this configuration, and the reported epsilon is not an upper bound. Additionally, `build_sampler`'s own docstring at :217-220 asserts the opposite of what it does: "Privacy-derived sampler parameters (``bands``, paper-``p``) are read off the built ``mf`` recipe / amplifier ... so the runtime sampler cannot desync from the accountant."
findings.failure_scenario: `DPTrainingArguments(privacy_noise_mechanism="mf_band", sampling_mode="poisson", privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={"bands": 10}, train_batch_size=256, ...)` on a 50k-row dataset for 1000 steps. Validation accepts it (_training_arguments.py:1048). Measured on the current tree: `build_amplifier_factory(sampling_mode='poisson', strategy=band_mf_strategy(bands=10), sample_rate=256/50000, n_steps=1000)(1.0)` returns `CyclicPoisson` with `num_groups=100` and reports `epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.355`; `build_sampler(sampling_mode='poisson', ...)` returns `PoissonSampler` with no `bands` attribute. Iterating that sampler for 1000 steps gives 206,254 consecutive-participation gaps of which 5.6% are smaller than `bands=10` and the minimum gap is 1 — i.e. the b-min-separation the accountant assumes is violated on 1 in 18 participation pairs. The sensitivity the accountant divides by is `BandMfStrategy.sensitivity(...) = ||coef|| = 1.0000` (which ignores its `min_sep`/`max_participations` arguments entirely, _band_mf.py:126-128), whereas the true sensitivity of the same 10-banded Toeplitz C under min_sep=1 is `minsep_sensitivity_squared(coef, 1, k)**0.5` = 1.92 at k=2, 4.47 at k=5, 7.97 at k=10 and 11.82 at k=18 (18 was the largest participation count actually observed in the run). The deployed noise is therefore calibrated against a sensitivity that is up to ~12x too small, and only 100 of the 1000 rounds are composed. The reported epsilon is silently far below the true one.

findings.fix_sketch: Either remove "poisson" from `_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS["mf_band"]`, or make `build_sampler` dispatch mf_band+poisson to `CyclicPoissonSampler(..., bands=int(mf.strategy.bands))` (the sampler the accountant actually models — currently reachable only through the `cyclic_poisson` mode, which no mechanism allows). Separately, make `BandMfStrategy.sensitivity` raise (or return the true min-sep sensitivity) when `min_sep < bands`, so a b-banded strategy cannot be priced at its single-participation column norm under a sampler that gives no separation. Related open issues #320 ("Bind runtime sampling to amplification accounting") and #356 ("Emit and require a sampler-accounting contract") cover this class; the delta reported here is that the trainer ships a concrete, validated, explicitly-commented mispairing and that the dispatch docstring asserts the invariant it breaks.

findings.title: mu-GDP one-run audit substitutes v_k = 0.5 for every rank past 2000 and calls it "conservative" — it is the anti-conservative direction under Xiang et al. Theorem 3, inflating the audited mu lower bound
findings.claim: `_p_value` computes exact `v_k` for only `r_prime = min(r, _MAX_EXACT_RANKS)` ranks and sets `n_trunc = r - r_prime` ranks to `v_k = 0.5`, annotated `# truncated ranks use v_k = 0.5 (conservative)` (:38) and `n_trunc = r - r_prime  # truncated ranks use v_k = 0.5` (:333). The bound it implements is cited as "Xiang et al. 2025, Theorem 3" (:377) with `v_k` from "Eq. 12" (:342). arXiv:2509.08704 Theorem 3 states `Pr_{B,M}[event_u] <= Pr[sum_{k=n-r+1}^{n} V_k <= u]` with `V_k ~ Bernoulli(v_k)` and `v_k` given by the integral in its Eq. (25) (the code's `_compute_v_k` reproduces that integral correctly). Because `sigmoid(-|L|) <= 0.5` always, `v_k <= 0.5`, so `0.5` is an UPPER bound on each true `v_k`. `Pr[sum V_k <= u]` is monotonically DECREASING in the `v_k`, so substituting the upper bound makes the computed p-value SMALLER than the true bound — the result is no longer an upper bound on `Pr[event_u]` and is not a valid p-value. `_mu_at` returns `mu_lo`, the largest mu at which the p-value stays below `significance` (i.e. the largest rejected mu), so an under-stated p-value rejects too much and reports an inflated mu-hat, i.e. an audited epsilon LOWER bound that the data does not support. The comment at :37-39 ("Higher ranks ... have lower error probability (more confident). Truncated low-confidence ranks use v_k = 0.5 (conservative). ... covers the top 20 % for n = 10K, which dominates the Chernoff sum") is wrong on both counts: the substitution is anti-conservative, and the truncated block dominates the sum, not the exact block.
findings.failure_scenario: `_best_r_u` always returns `r = m = n_in + n_out` (_estimate.py:147, 152, 161), so any audit with more than 2000 canaries truncates. Measured on the current tree at significance 0.05: with m = r = 3000 canaries and u = 900 errors, the shipped code reports mu-hat = 1.0563 while the same search with exact `v_k` (`_MAX_EXACT_RANKS` raised) gives 0.9313. With r = 4000, u = 1100, n = 20000 the gap is 1.0688 vs 0.4875 — a 2.2x inflation of the audited mu. Directly at the p-value level, n=20000, r=8000, mu=1.0, u=1396: exact p-value 0.0909 (would NOT reject at 0.05) vs truncated p-value 0.0 (rejects). Because `docs/user-guide/auditing.md:5-6` tells users "If the audited epsilon exceeds the theoretical epsilon, there is likely a bug in the implementation", the practical consequence is a false privacy-violation alarm on a correct implementation; in the strong-attack regime (u below ~0.5*(r-2000)) the same defect makes the p-value stay below significance for every finite mu and `_mu_at` raises RuntimeError instead (:80-89).

Delta-window commit 611faf51 ("fix(auditing): cap mu-GDP _mu_at search to stop infinite hang", #299) touched exactly this code, added a `Raises: RuntimeError ... which truncated ranks (v_k = 0.5) can cause` docstring, and left the wrong-direction bound and the "(conservative)" comment in place
findings.fix_sketch: Use a valid LOWER bound on the truncated ranks' v_k instead of 0.5 — e.g. `min(v_k)` over the exactly-computed block, or 0 (crudely valid, since dropping ranks only removes Bernoullis from the sum and increases `Pr[sum <= u]`). Better: compute `v_k` on a coarse rank grid and interpolate downward, or raise `_MAX_EXACT_RANKS` with a chunked integration so no substitution is needed. At minimum, fix the comment and refuse to return a mu-hat when `r > _MAX_EXACT_RANKS` rather than silently returning an inflated one. Related open issues #376 ("Calibrate one-run auditing under the null") and #327, and July's OPQ-003/OPQ-004/OPQ-024 root-cause note; the delta here is the measured magnitude and direction plus the fact that the in-window remediation entrenched the wrong-direction bound in a new docstring.

findings.title: Truncated-Poisson accounting silently switches the adjacency relation to Ganesh's dataset-size-dependent add-or-remove-1-of-n, and its sole citation is the unresolvable key [Gan25]
findings.claim: The truncated-Poisson PLD is documented as `Uses the mixture formula from \[Gan25\]` (:20) and `Hockey-stick divergence for truncated Poisson (mixture formula from \[Gan25\])` (:125). `Gan25` appears three times in the repository (twice here, once in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_cross_validation.py:369) and is defined nowhere — no bibliography entry, no arXiv id, no author name. The actual source is Arun Ganesh, "Tighter Privacy Analysis for Truncated Poisson Sampling", arXiv:2508.15089, which appears nowhere in the repository (the only hit for that id in the checkout is inside the vendored `.venv/lib/.../dp_accounting/dp_event.py`). The formula itself is faithfully implemented (verified below), but the paper's Theorem 3.1 is stated for a RESTRICTED adjacency: "we start with the simplest version of our result, which uses a restricted version of the add-or-remove-1-of-n adjacency ... Normally, the add-remove adjacency says D and D' are adjacent if D' is a size |D|-1 subset of D or vice-versa, without a restriction on |D|. Our privacy guarantee depends on |D|, so we need to restrict to D,D' pairs of a specific size n." It then warns: "if we are composing M_{B,p,sigma} with other mechanisms, we need to be careful about using this result. Hence, we recommend avoiding the use of this result in these settings." Opaque documents a different convention — `docs/user-guide/dp-concepts.md:373` "Opaque uses the **add-or-remove** convention" — states nothing about the n-dependence anywhere in `docs/reference/accounting.md:238-249`, `docs/mechanisms/index.md:88`, or the factory docstring, and freely composes the truncated process with unrelated mechanisms.
findings.failure_scenario: A user writes `step = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(0.8), sample_rate=256/50000, truncated_batch_size=256, dataset_size=50000)` (verbatim the example at docs/reference/accounting.md:250-259) and then composes it with any other release: `acc = Accountant() | step | dpsgd_acc.gaussian(2.0)` runs without warning and reports eps = 1.994 at delta=1e-5 (measured on the current tree). The published epsilon is only meaningful under add-or-remove-1-of-n with |D| = 50000 treated as public and fixed, and the paper explicitly recommends against using the result in exactly this composed setting. A reader who follows the code comment cannot discover this because `[Gan25]` resolves to nothing.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/truncated_poisson.rs:20 — `/// Uses the mixture formula from \[Gan25\]:`; :125 — `/// Hockey-stick divergence for truncated Poisson (mixture formula from \[Gan25\]).`
`grep -rn "Gan25" .` → 3 hits, all uses, no definition; `grep -rn "2508.15089"` over the repository source → 0 hits (only the vendored dp_accounting package)

arXiv:2508.15089 Section 3.1 (PDF text): "we start with the simplest version of our result, which uses a restricted version of the add-or-remove-1-of-n adjacency ... Our privacy guarantee depends on |D|, so we need to restrict to D,D' pairs of a specific size n"

arXiv:2508.15089, "Privacy of n" paragraph: "if we are composing M_{B,n,sigma} with other mechanisms, we need to be careful about using this result. Hence, we recommend avoiding the use of this result in these settings, and even when using this result just to run M_{B,n,sigma} with no other mechanisms, one should be precise when stating the formal privacy guarantees."
docs/user-guide/dp-concepts.md:373 — "Opaque uses the **add-or-remove** convention"; docs/reference/accounting.md:238-249 documents the truncated form with no adjacency caveat
Measured on the current tree: `Accountant() | poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01, truncated_batch_size=600, dataset_size=50000) | gaussian(2.0)` → epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.9944, no warning

Math verified correct: `truncation_probability` = Pr[Binom(n-1,q) >= B] matches the paper's r-split; `conditional_sampling_probability` = Pr[Binom(n,p) >= B+1] * B / n / p_trunc matches the paper's Section 3.4 closed form exactly (derived independently via C(n,s+1) = C(n-1,s)*n/(s+1)); component 2 (Adjacency::Replace at sigma/2) numerically dominates the paper's one-sided pair by 1.00-19x over a sweep of sigma in {1,2}, q in {0.001..0.5}, eps in {0.5..4} — conservative, never smaller
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `[Gan25]` with the full citation (Arun Ganesh, "Tighter Privacy Analysis for Truncated Poisson Sampling", arXiv:2508.15089) in truncated_poisson.rs and the test, and state in the `poisson(..., truncated_batch_size=)` docstring and docs/reference/accounting.md that the truncated form's guarantee is under add-or-remove-1-of-n with `dataset_size` public and fixed, that it is not the same adjacency as the plain-Poisson form, and that the source recommends against composing it with unrelated mechanisms. Optionally warn when a truncated-Poisson process is composed with a process of a different family.

findings.title: lambda-CGD sensitivity is documented as "Theorem 1, eq 15 of the paper" — Theorem 1's hypotheses do not cover the default normalized mechanism, and eq (15) is a utility metric, not a sensitivity
findings.claim: The doc says "The sensitivity formula (Theorem 1, eq 15 of the paper) has a closed-form expression in terms of λ, min_sep, and max_participations." In arXiv:2601.22334 (Kalinin, McKenna, Pagh, Lampert, "DP-λCGD"), Theorem 1 is a restatement of Kalinin & Lampert (2024) Theorem 2 and reads "Let C be a lower triangular Toeplitz matrix with decreasing non-negative entries c_0 >= c_1 >= ... >= c_{n-1} >= 0. Then, under b-min-separation, the sensitivity is given by sens_{k,b}(C) = ||sum_{j=0}^{k-1} C[:, jb+1]||_2" — a generic statement with no closed form in λ, and the paper explicitly says of the column-normalized variant (which is Opaque's DEFAULT, `normalized: bool = True`): "sensitivity Theorem 1 cannot be applied directly. In this work, we generalize the sensitivity theorem specifically for the normalized DP-λCGD in the following theorem. Lemma 8. The sensitivity of the column-normalized DP-λCGD ... (12)". Eq. (15) is not a sensitivity at all: it is "The squared maximum row l2-norm of the matrix A C_λ^{-1} is ||A C_λ^{-1}||^2_{2→∞} = 1 + (1-λ)^2 (n-1)" — a MaxSE utility quantity appearing inside the proof of Lemma 2. The closed-form λ-CGD sensitivity is eq (14), also inside that proof, and it applies to the UNnormalized matrix. A reviewer checking `LambdaCgdStrategy.sensitivity` against the cited pointer is sent to a theorem whose hypotheses the default configuration does not satisfy and to an equation that computes something else.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer (or a downstream auditor following the repo's own differential-privacy-review protocol, which requires following the citation to the primary source) opens arXiv:2601.22334, finds Theorem 1 stating a generic min-sep formula for decreasing non-negative Toeplitz matrices, finds eq (15) is a row-norm of the noising matrix, and cannot confirm or refute what `_native().lambda_cgd_normalized_sensitivity_squared(...)` computes. The single sentence that would let them do so — that the default `normalized=True` path is Lemma 8 / eq (12) and the `normalized=False` path is eq (14) — is absent.
evidence: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:70-73 — "The sensitivity formula (Theorem 1, eq 15 of the paper) has a closed-form expression in terms of λ, min_sep, and max_participations."

arXiv:2601.22334 Theorem 1 (PDF text): "Theorem 1 (Theorem 2 from Kalinin and Lampert [2024]). Let C be a lower triangular Toeplitz matrix with decreasing non-negative entries c_0 >= c_1 >= ... >= c_{n-1} >= 0. Then, under b-min-separation, the sensitivity is given by sens_{k,b}(C) = ||sum_{j=0}^{k-1} C[:,jb+1]||_2, (3)"

arXiv:2601.22334: "sensitivity Theorem 1 cannot be applied directly. In this work, we generalize the sensitivity theorem specifically for the normalized DP-λCGD in the following theorem. Lemma 8. The sensitivity of the column-normalized DP-λCGD with strategy matrix C_λ and column norms D = diag(d_1,...,d_n) is given by sens_{k,b}(C_λ D^{-1}) = ||sum_{j=0}^{k-1} (C_λ D^{-1})_{:,jb+1}||_2 . (12)"
arXiv:2601.22334 eq (15): "The squared maximum row l2-norm of the matrix A C_λ^{-1} is ||A C_λ^{-1}||^2_{2→∞} = 1 + (1-λ)^2 (n-1). (15)"
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_lambda_cgd.py:171-181 — `normalized: bool = True` is the default and routes to `lambda_cgd_normalized_sensitivity_squared`

Implementation itself verified CORRECT and tighter than eq (14): at λ=0.9, n=120, b=4, k=8 the Rust unnormalized value is 146.373, matching an independent dense-matrix brute force to 8 digits, while eq (14)'s infinite-n simplification gives 128.509; the normalized value 27.811 also matches brute force, and an exhaustive search over all min-sep patterns (n=20, b=4, k=4, λ in {0.3,0.7,0.95}) confirms the (0,b,2b,...) pattern the code assumes is the true maximiser
findings.fix_sketch: Point at Lemma 8 / eq (12) for the default `normalized=True` path and at eq (14) (inside the proof of Lemma 2) for `normalized=False`, and note that Theorem 1's decreasing-non-negative-Toeplitz hypothesis is what the normalized case does not satisfy directly.

findings.title: BISR implements Lemma 1 with alpha silently pinned to 1 and enforces none of its 0 <= beta < alpha <= 1 hypothesis, while the sibling BSR strategy enforces exactly that hypothesis
findings.claim: `_bisr_inverse_coefficients_cached` is documented as "BISR inverse square-root coefficients (Lemma 1, arxiv:2505.12128)" and computes `c_k = sum_j r_j * beta^j * r_{k-j}` with the docstring note "For alpha=1". arXiv:2505.12128 Lemma 1 reads "The inverse square root of the matrix A^{-1/2}_{alpha,beta} defined in (4), for 0 <= beta < alpha <= 1, is C^{-1}_{alpha,beta} = ... where c~^{alpha,beta}_k = sum_{j=0}^{k} r~_j beta^j r~_{k-j} alpha^{k-j}". The code drops the `alpha^{k-j}` factor (valid only at alpha = 1, which it never exposes or documents) and drops the hypothesis: `BisrStrategy.__post_init__` (:163-173) validates only `bandwidth >= 2` and the `inv_coefficients` length, and `beta` is exposed as the unvalidated `momentum` field (:159, :178). `bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4, momentum=1.5)` is accepted. Notably `_bsr.py:72-101` (`_validate_bsr_hyperparams`) enforces the identical hypothesis for the sibling mechanism with explicit `BSR v1 requires beta in [0, 1)` / `requires alpha in (0, 1]` / `requires alpha > beta` errors, and the Rust `bisr.rs:149-168 validate_common` validates a *different*, Python-unreachable `momentum` argument to `[0, 1)` — so the parameter that is checked is the one that is never passed, and the one that matters is unchecked. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:64-68 reproduces the same alpha-free formula and hypothesis-free framing.
findings.failure_scenario: `bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4, momentum=1.0)` (a natural carry-over from `band_mf_strategy`, whose `momentum` defaults to 1.0) or `momentum=1.5` is accepted silently. At momentum=1.5, bandwidth=8 the recovered strategy column grows to 2.5e8 over 64 steps instead of decaying, producing a numerically absurd mechanism that the user has no signal about. I could NOT turn this into an epsilon error: an exhaustive search over all min-sep participation patterns (n=18, b=3, k=4, beta in {0, 0.9, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}) shows `bisr_sensitivity_squared` still returns the exact maximum, and the recovered C stays non-negative (so the balls-in-bins Lemma 3.2 hypothesis also survives). The defect is therefore an unenforced documented precondition and an inconsistency with BSR, not a demonstrated privacy break.

findings.fix_sketch: Add `0.0 <= momentum < 1.0` to `BisrStrategy.__post_init__` (matching `_validate_bsr_hyperparams`), rename the field or document it as the paper's `beta`, state in the module and in docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md that alpha is pinned to 1, and either expose alpha or drop it from the reproduced formula.

findings.title: `sampling_mode="cyclic_poisson"` is a documented, implemented sampling mode that no mechanism's allow-list accepts, so the only sampler matching the cited BandMF cyclic-Poisson theorem is unreachable from the trainer
findings.claim: `"cyclic_poisson"` is a member of `_SAMPLING_MODES` (:161), has a full `build_sampler` branch that constructs `CyclicPoissonSampler(..., bands=int(mf.strategy.bands))` (_dpftrl.py:282-294), and is advertised to users as a settable value in docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:124. But it appears in no entry of `_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS` (:185-195), so `__post_init__` (:1048-1054) rejects it for every value of `privacy_noise_mechanism`. Verified on the current tree: `[m for m,v in _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS.items() if "cyclic_poisson" in v]` == `[]`. There is also no `build_amplifier_factory` branch for it (it would hit the `else: raise ValueError` at _dpftrl.py:175-179).
findings.failure_scenario: A user reads training-arguments.md:124, sets `sampling_mode="cyclic_poisson"` for `privacy_noise_mechanism="mf_band"` to get the cyclic-Poisson participation pattern that `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson` and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:75-92 describe, and gets `ValueError: sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson' is not valid for privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band'; allowed: ['b_min_sep', 'poisson']`. The suggested alternative, `"poisson"`, is the mispairing reported as the first finding above.
evidence: Run on current tree: `from opaque.api.transformers.trainer._training_arguments import _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS, _SAMPLING_MODES` → `"cyclic_poisson" in _SAMPLING_MODES` is True, `[m for m,v in _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS.items() if "cyclic_poisson" in v]` is `[]`
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:282-294 — live `cyclic_poisson` branch building `CyclicPoissonSampler`
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:174-179 — `build_amplifier_factory` raises for any mode other than poisson/b_min_sep/balls_in_bins
docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:124 — lists `"cyclic_poisson"` among "explicit values ... validated against the mechanism's allow-list"
findings.fix_sketch: Add `"cyclic_poisson"` to `_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS["mf_band"]` (and `mf_identity`) together with a `build_amplifier_factory` branch that returns `ftrl_acc.poisson(...)`, or remove the mode, its sampler branch and its docs entry.

findings.title: `ftrl_acc.poisson` documents `sample_rate` as the per-step probability without saying it is measured against the band group of size |D|/bands, unlike the sampler that consumes it
findings.claim: The factory documents `sample_rate: Per-step Poisson sampling probability ∈ (0, 1]` (:265) and the module header says the run "divide[s] into ``num_groups = ceil(n_steps / bands)`` independent groups" (:3-5) — using "groups" for the cycle count while `CyclicPoissonSampler` uses "group" for the `bands` data partitions. The cited Theorem 4 of arXiv:2306.08153 is explicit that the reduction is to "k sensitivity-kappa queries on a dataset of size m-check = floor(m/b)", i.e. the sampling probability is relative to the band group, not the full dataset. `CyclicPoissonSampler` documents this correctly (`expected_batch_size` = `|D| / bands * sample_rate`, sampling/_poisson.py:186-190), but the accounting side does not, and the two names disagree.
findings.failure_scenario: A user carrying over the DP-SGD habit sets `sample_rate = batch/|D|` for a BandMF run with bands=8. Accounting and sampler stay consistent (both use the same q, so epsilon is still valid), but the realised batch is 8x smaller than intended: measured on the current tree, `CyclicPoissonSampler(50000 rows, sample_rate=256/50000, bands=8, n_steps=400)` yields a mean batch of 32.1 while the trainer's `normalize_by` is the nominal 256 (`_dp_trainer.py:1379` computes `sample_rate = expected_batch_size / dataset_size` with no `bands` factor and `:4162` passes `normalize_by=expected_batch_size`), so the mean-gradient estimate is 8x too small against unchanged noise.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:265 — `sample_rate: Per-step Poisson sampling probability ``∈ (0, 1]``.`

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:186-190 — `"""Expected batch size: ``|group| * sample_rate`` (before truncation)."""` with `avg_group_size = self.num_examples / self.bands`
arXiv:2306.08153 Theorem 4: "...on a dataset of size m-check = floor(m/b-check) using the Gaussian mechanism, where each query is run on a random subset of examples of size B"
Measured: CyclicPoissonSampler(50000, sample_rate=256/50000, bands=8, n_steps=400) → mean realised batch 32.1 (property `expected_batch_size` = 32.0)
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1379 — `sample_rate = expected_batch_size / dataset_size` (no bands factor)
findings.fix_sketch: State in the `poisson()` docstring that `sample_rate` is the per-example inclusion probability within the active band group (population `|D|/bands`), so the expected batch is `|D| * sample_rate / bands`, and rename `num_groups` in the module header to `num_cycles`/`num_participations` to stop it colliding with the sampler's `bands` groups.

clean_areas: BandMF cyclic-Poisson accounting math (packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py) checks out against arXiv:2306.08153 Theorem 4 when the matching sampler is used: `num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands)` is exactly the participation count k of a worst-case example under Algorithm 2's cyclic partition; `BandMfStrategy.sensitivity` returning `||coef||` is right because `optimize()` normalises the coefficients to unit L2 (`return params / torch.linalg.norm(params)`, _toeplitz.py:690), so the effective noise multiplier is `nm` exactly; the K-prefix rounding up to a band boundary is the conservative direction. The paper's Theorem 4 uses fixed-size-B sampling (Algorithm 2) rather than Poisson, but the paper states "we focus on amplification by sampling with fixed batch size in this section, but give a more general statement in Appendix F", so the Poisson variant is within the cited scope; the block-decomposition argument (b-banded C plus b-separated participations ⇒ each participation touches a disjoint row block ⇒ k independent subsampled Gaussians at sensitivity ||c||) is sound and I re-derived it independently.

CyclicPoissonSampler matches that accounting when paired directly (library level): step i activates group i % bands, each eligible example is Bernoulli(sample_rate), so a worst-case example gets exactly ceil(n_steps/bands) opportunities separated by exactly `bands`, and `sample_rate` is the within-group rate the per-group PLD assumes. docs/user-guide/sampling.md:487 documents the correct pairing.

Balls-in-Bins dominating pair: verified verbatim against arXiv:2410.06266 Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.2, including the |C| absolute values ("where |C| is the matrix whose entries are the absolute values of corresponding entry in C") and the add/remove direction split. The Rust MC accountant samples BOTH directions (`sample_privacy_loss_remove` / `sample_privacy_loss_add`, monte_carlo.rs:59-140) and builds an asymmetric PLD, and the simultaneous confidence band explicitly union-bounds over "every rank and adjacency direction" (monte_carlo.rs:337-345) — matching the paper's remark that add-and-remove costs a factor 2 in the failure probability. The Identity-strategy collapse to 1-out-of-b random allocation at sigma_eff = sigma/sqrt(E) is algebraically correct (orthogonal m_i of equal norm sqrt(E) ⇒ G = E·I_b; rescaling by 1/sqrt(E) is a bijection preserving privacy loss). `n_steps` must be a multiple of `num_bins`, so the Definition-3.1 n = b·E hypothesis is enforced.

Truncated-Poisson formulas: `truncation_probability` = Pr[Binom(n-1,q) >= B] and `conditional_sampling_probability` = Pr[Binom(n,p) >= B+1] * B / (n * p_trunc) reproduce arXiv:2508.15089 Theorem 3.1 and its Section 3.4 closed form exactly (I re-derived the identity p*Pr[Binom(n-1,p)=s]/(s+1) = Pr[Binom(n,p)=s+1]/n by hand). The labelled-mixture decomposition (1-p_trunc)*delta_1 + p_trunc*delta_2 is what Section 3.4 prescribes ("a 'mixture of mechanisms' where the choice of mechanism in the mixture is made public"). Component 1's max(ADD, REMOVE) and component 2's use of Adjacency::Replace at sigma/2 are both conservative: numerically, component 2 dominates the paper's one-sided pair by factors 1.00-19x across sigma in {1,2}, q in {0.001,0.01,0.1,0.5}, eps in {0.5,1,2,4}, never smaller. Only the adjacency semantics and the dangling citekey are reported.

Feldman & Shenfeld (arXiv:2602.17284) citation in packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs and pld/realization.rs: authors, title and the paper's PLD-realization framing all verified against the abstract. The note at realization.rs:3-9 is unusually careful and correct — the transform is stated for first-order stochastic domination, which is strictly stronger than the hockey-stick tightness Connect-the-Dots gives, so CTD outputs must not feed it; `disc_dist` supplies a CDF-binned, stochastically dominating alternative instead.

BLT citations: `pillutla_score()` = sum(output_scale/buf_decay) matches arXiv:2504.21413 Theorem 1(a) exactly ("if sum_{i} alpha_i/lambda_i < 1, then lambda-hat_i in (0,1) for each i"), and the docstring's "Score < 1 ensures well-behaved inverse" is a faithful reading. `from_rational_approx_to_sqrt_x` citing Proposition 4.5 of arXiv:2404.16706v2 is an initialisation heuristic, not a privacy claim.

BSR: `_r_sequence` r_k = |binom(-1/2,k)| with r_k = r_{k-1}(k-0.5)/k and `c_j = sum_i alpha^{j-i} r_{j-i} r_i beta^i` match arXiv:2405.13763 Theorem 1 (the absolute value is required for the Theorem-2 monotone-non-negative regime and the docstring says so). `_validate_bsr_hyperparams` enforces the paper regime 0 <= beta < alpha <= 1 plus non-negativity and monotone non-increase — the preconditions Theorem 2 needs — with explicit error messages.

BISR sensitivity: `bisr_sensitivity_squared` and `bisr_normalized_sensitivity_squared` return the exact maximum over min-sep participation patterns. Verified by exhaustive enumeration of every valid pattern (n=18, b=3, k=4) and by start-offset sweeps at n=24, b=4, k=6, for beta in {0, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, -0.5} — the (0,b,2b,...) pattern the code assumes is always the argmax, even outside the paper's parameter regime. The recovered strategy column stays non-negative for every beta tested, so the balls-in-bins non-negativity hypothesis holds.

lambda-CGD implementation: `lambda_cgd_sensitivity_squared` and `lambda_cgd_normalized_sensitivity_squared` match an independent dense-matrix brute force to 8 significant figures (lambda in {0.5,0.9}, (n,b,k) in {(200,10,10),(120,4,8)}) and are TIGHTER than the paper's eq (14) asymptotic form; an exhaustive min-sep pattern search (n=20, b=4, k=4) confirms the assumed maximiser for the normalized case that arXiv:2601.22334 Lemma 8 asserts. `_column_norm` = sqrt((1-lambda^{2(n-t)})/(1-lambda^2)) is the exact column norm of Toeplitz(lambda^k), and `_lambda_cgd_row_l2` = d_t*sqrt(1+lambda^2) is the exact row norm of D C^{-1}. `lambda_ in [0,1)` is enforced, keeping C non-negative for the BnB dominating pair.

Auditing attack citation: `loss_scores(..., reference_scores=...)` returning `current - reference` = loss(w0) - loss(wt) matches arXiv:2305.08846 Algorithm 3 line 9 verbatim ("Define Score(x_i, w_l) = l(w_0, x_i) - l(w_l, x_i)"). `coin_flip` as i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) matches Algorithm 3 line 3.

`_compute_v_k` itself is a faithful implementation of arXiv:2509.08704 Eq. (25): the binomial order-statistic weight C(n,k)(k-1)!/(n-k)!, the mixture density f_Y = (P+Q)/2, F_Y in |L|-sorted space and the sigmoid(-|L|) Bayes-error factor all line up; the log-space integration and the k=1 / k=n edge guards are correct. Only the rank truncation applied on top of it is unsound.

arXiv id integrity: every id cited from opaque-accounting, opaque-dpftrl, opaque-auditing and opaque-dpsgd source resolves to a real paper whose title matches the gloss beside it — checked 2306.08153, 2404.16706, 2408.08868, 2405.13763, 2505.12128, 2601.22334, 2509.08704, 2305.08846, 2412.16802, 2504.21413, 2502.06597, 2506.08201, 2507.06969, 2405.15913, 2211.17230, 2602.17284, 2211.06530, 2410.06266, 2602.09338, 2511.07843, 2605.27292, plus the 2026-dated ids 2603.12201, 2604.01694, 2605.27292, 2604.07622, 2602.04118, 2602.04562, 2510.01149, 2511.07843, 2512.14527, 2512.07703, 2512.02010, 2509.15974 (all HTTP 200 with matching titles). No fabricated identifier found. Author attributions spot-checked and correct for Feldman & Shenfeld (2602.17284), Dong & Ganesh (2602.09338), Kalinin/McKenna/Upadhyay/Lampert (2505.12128), Kalinin/McKenna/Pagh/Lampert (2601.22334), Dagreou & Bellet (2605.27292), Chooi/Cong/Li/Sun (2511.07843), Choquette-Choo/Ganesh/Haque/Steinke/Thakurta (2410.06266) — the July OPQ-161/165/166/167 attribution defects are not reproducible on this tree.

`b_min_sep` amplification: `participation_p_from_per_example_rate(p0, bands) = p0/(1 - p0*(bands-1))` is the exact inverse of the stationary participation probability p/(1 + p(b-1)) of the b-cooldown renewal chain that BMinSepSampler realises, and `min_sep`/`max_participations` on the BMinSep process (bands, ceil(n/bands)) are the values the paper's model implies. Title of arXiv:2602.09338 matches verbatim.

DP-AdamW bias-correction citation (docs/user-guide/optimizers.md:160-161, docs/reference/optimizers.md:95): arXiv:2511.07843 exists with the stated authors. The docs attribute only the algorithm to it and hedge every utility statement to the repo's own sweeps, so the paper's contrary empirical finding (that DP-AdamW-BC decreases accuracy) is not misrepresented as its endorsement.

Not re-examined in depth because Phase A already verified them and I found no contradicting evidence: Algorithms 3/4 of 2306.08153 in noise/_sensitivity.py, Algorithms 2/3 of 2408.08868 and Lemmas 5.2/5.3 of 2404.16706 in _blt_math.py, Theorem 2 of 2405.13763 in _toeplitz.minsep_sensitivity_squared, and the 2207.04380 / 2507.06969 pointers in the accounting core.
